Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear constraints and the doc. We can definitely run a compact POC that covers prompt review, routing policy validation, and a smoke load run.

Suggested approach (quick):
- Kickoff: 30–45m alignment (goals, success criteria, roles).
- Hands-on blocks (90m each):
  * Window A — US-focused: 09:00–10:30 PDT (US engineering lead + Redwood infra)
  * Window B — EU overlap: 14:00–15:30 CET (EU product + Redwood runtime team)
  * Window C — APAC-friendly: 22:00–23:30 CET (this hits APAC early morning)

We can rotate the order so no team always gets the late slot; i.e., Week 1: A/B/C, Week 2: B/C/A. That keeps a predictable rotation for on-call coverage.

Action items I propose before kickoff:
- ACME: share 2–3 representative prompts and a sample dataset (preferably obfuscated).
- Redwood: prepare a lightweight routing matrix and a one-hour smoke script for concurrent token throughput.
- All: fill the quick availability poll Marissa will share.

Cc'ing Marissa to drop a calendar poll / invite. If those windows look wrong, tell us which specific local times to target and we’ll adapt.

Cheers,

- APAC can do early-morning CET slots (02:00–05:00 CET) — that maps to ~10:00–13:00 JST; they prefer single 90m block once per week rather than back-to-back nights.

Preferred pattern from our side: Week 1: US morning (A) + EU overlap (B). Week 2: rotate so APAC gets the earlier window (C) and US/EU shift accordingly. That means the late-cet slot Rishi suggested should be minimized.

If we can lock one kickoff this week for alignment (30–45m), we can then start the rotating hands-on blocks next week. Our team is available for a kickoff on Wed or Thu — either 16:00–16:45 UTC on Wed or 14:00–14:45 UTC on Thu. Which works for you?
